paper.title: Preaching to the converted: Cultural intermediaries and cultural consumer behavior
paper.code_data_availability: Data availability: The administrative data used in this study are available at https://www.dst.dk/en/TilSalg/Forskningsservice/Dataadgang with the permission of Statistics Denmark. …

registers.name_in_paper: registry data on the universe of library book loans from Danish public libraries
variables_mentioned: which book it was (title and author)

registers.name_in_paper: the Danish national registries (highest education of the person loaning a book)
variables_mentioned: highest educational level (Less than high school, high school, 1–3 y. college, 5 + y. college)

registers.name_in_paper: previous library use of the person loaning a book (loans of books from libraries in 2020)
registers.role: subgroup definition (cultural capital: previous reading behavior)
variables_mentioned: loan of books from libraries in 2020

registers.name_in_paper: dataset on major Danish literary awards announced from July 2021 to December 2022
variables_mentioned: whether the final decision is made by an appointed committee or by vote

registers.name_in_paper: dataset of literary reviews in national Danish newspapers obtained from the website Bog.nu
Cultural Participation Survey [Kulturvaneundersogelsen] administered by Statistics Denmark
registers.role: supplementary subgroup definition (survey-based measure of reading preferences, subsample)

linkages: Loan records linked to the person loaning the book through unique personal identifiers and merged with the Danish national registries for highest education and previous library use
Awards merged to the loan data both by title and by author, giving an effect on the award-winning title and a spill-over effect on other books by the same author
Literary reviews merged to the loan data by author; only the spill-over sample (other books by the reviewed author) is analysed

sample.universe: The universe of library book loans from Danish public libraries, May 2021 to December 2022 (post Covid-19 lockdowns); adults’ loans of books, excluding children’s books
sample.unit_of_observation: Book title by week (87 weeks); in the stratified analyses, book title by week by individual group (education or previous reading behavior)
selection_rules: Adults’ loans of books only; children’s books excluded
Danish rather than international awards, because loans of books not in Danish are rare and awarded books are often not yet translated
Books enter the sample only if they receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point (award analyses)
Titles enter the dataset the first week a loan is observed, as they are assumed not to be available previously
Control group = nominated/short-listed titles plus titles that go on to receive an award in a later period (not-yet-treated)
For the review analyses, only the spill-over sample (other books by the reviewed author) is used, because reviews are published around the time the book becomes available
sample.period: May 2021 to December 2022 (loans); awards and reviews from July 2021 to December 2022
sample.n_observations: Table 1: Award title N total 4163; Award author N total 40,336; Review author N total 264,183 (87 weeks in each)

construction_notes: Award title analysis: 14 award events, 66 titles, 18 award-winning titles (titles in both Danish and the original language are included), 48 nominated titles (Table 1)
Award author analysis: 12 award events, 546 titles, 180 winner titles, 366 nominated titles (Table 1)
Review author analysis: 210 review events, 3319 titles (Table 1)
N total does not equal N weeks x N titles because titles only enter the dataset the first week a loan is observed

Awards classified as high cultural legitimacy if selected by an appointed committee and low cultural legitimacy if decided by vote; the deciding rule was whether the final decision was made by literary professionals
Reviews: normalized book score rating 1–100; positive = above the 75th percentile, mediocre = 25th-50th, negative = 0–25th
Previous reading behavior from 2020 loans: Non-readers = no loans; Occasional readers = 0–75th percentile (0–16 books); Avid readers = 75th+ percentile (17 books or more)
In the stratified analyses the outcome is scaled by the group population count and expressed as books loaned per week per 100,000 persons
Results are presented as dynamic event studies and as group-averaged ATTs for a short-term (4 weeks) and long-term (26 weeks / 6 months) post-period

links.pointer_quote: First, in line with previous research, I find that favorable signals from cultural intermediaries have a substantial impact – the loan of books increases following a book (or its author) receiving an award or a favorable newspaper review.

claims.statement: Over the 4 weeks following the event, literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award) increases number of loans per title per week of the award-winning title (“Award title”).

treatment.label: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award)

register_source.value: Dataset on major Danish literary awards announced from July 2021 to December 2022, merged to the library loan data by title and by author; not a Statistics Denmark register

definition.value: A binary, staggered treatment switching on in the week a major Danish literary award is announced. Awards announced July 2021 to December 2022 (e.g. De Gyldne Laurbær, Nordisk Råds Litteraturpris, Politikens Litteraturpris); 14 award events in the award-title analysis. Awards are merged to the loan data both by title and by author.

timing.value: Week in which the award is announced; treatment is staggered across award events (14 awards on 18 award-winning titles in the award-title analysis)

outcome.label: Number of loans per title per week of the award-winning title (“Award title”)

register_source.value: Registry data on the universe of library book loans from Danish public libraries (book title, author, date of loan, personal identifier of the loaner)

definition.value: Weekly count of loans of the book title from Danish public libraries. Table 2 states the unit as “Number of loans per title”; the text reports the effect as books per title per week.

timing.value: Weekly, in event time relative to the week of the award/review; aggregated over the first 4 weeks post-period

units.value: number of loans per title per week

magnitude.interpretation: The 4-week average increase in overall loans of 48.76 books per title per week for the treated titles and 8.70 for the spillover effects equates to an increase of, respectively, 80% and 107%.

estimand.target_population: Treated titles
estimand.time_horizon: group-averaged ATT over the 4 weeks after the award/review (short-term)

population.description: Loans of award-winning titles and of control titles (nominated/short-listed titles and titles awarded later), from the universe of adults’ loans of books (excluding children’s books) from Danish public libraries, May 2021 to December 2022
population.ages: Adults (the paper analyses adults’ loans of books, excluding children’s books)
population.period: May 2021 to December 2022 (loans); awards/reviews from July 2021 to December 2022
population.selection: Only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point enter the sample, so treated and control titles are “equally selected”; titles enter the dataset the first week a loan is observed.

identification.source_of_variation: Staggered timing of the announcement of major Danish literary awards (14 award events in the award-title analysis, July 2021 to December 2022), compared with nominated/short-listed titles and titles that win an award later (not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the award/review, loans of treated titles would have followed the same average time path as loans of the control titles (nominated/short-listed and not-yet-treated titles).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper motivates the control group as netting out average time trends and presents dynamic event studies with pre-award event time (Fig. 2, Fig. 4, Fig. 5); it notes awards occur about a year after publication, which enables estimating a pre-trend.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on ever being treated or nominated: only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point are compared, so that treated and control books are “equally selected” on the characteristics that make a book award-worthy.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the construction of the control group; no balance test is reported.

implies_edges.from: Sample inclusion: ever awarded/nominated (awards) or ever reviewed (reviews)
implies_edges.to: Number of loans per title per week of the award-winning title (“Award title”)

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference: the award/review event does not itself change loans of the control titles (the paper concedes that nominated control titles are “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Robustness analysis dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3 and Appendix Fig. A4); results reported as robust.

implies_edges.from: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award)
implies_edges.to: Loans of control titles (nominated / not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: loans do not respond to the award/review before the week it is announced or published.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Not tested directly; the event-study figures display pre-event event-time estimates.

implies_edges.from: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award)
implies_edges.to: Number of loans per title per week of the award-winning title (“Award title”) (pre-announcement weeks)

key_assumptions.assumption: Libraries do not differentially increase the physical/digital supply of award-winning books relative to control books in a way that generates the loan increase.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued rather than tested: the paper says library book purchasing agreements are a fairly slow process that cannot explain spikes in loans a few weeks after an award.

threats_discussed: Non-random timing of awards (awards may be announced when loans would be high anyway)
Non-random selection of books into awards (genre, quality, style)
Nominated control titles are themselves “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced
Supply constraints on physical and digital loans, and possible library supply responses to awards
robustness_checks: Dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A4)
Adding a third “mixed” cultural-legitimacy category (Appendix Figure A1)
Restricting to individuals who used libraries at least once in 2020 (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A5)
Measuring the outcome in logs rather than levels (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A9)
Survey-based measure of reading practices from the Cultural Participation Survey (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Fig. A2-A3)
Narrower cultural-elite definitions: PhD degree and top 5th percentile of library users (Appendix Tables A1 and A2, Appendix Fig. A8)
Stratification by income and by cultural/economic capital of occupation (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Figure A3)
unresolved_confounders: The effect cannot be decomposed into the direct effect of individuals noticing the signal and the indirect effect of institutions (libraries, bookstores, media) amplifying it

estimator.value: Staggered difference-in-differences, Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021) group-time ATT, aggregated to a group-averaged ATT

estimation.specification: Staggered DID on weekly loans per title; group-time ATT(g,t) à la Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021) with nominated/short-listed and not-yet-treated titles as controls, aggregated to a group-averaged ATT over the first 4 weeks post-period. No estimating equation is printed in the paper.

source_table.value: Table 2, row “Award title / Main effect”, column “Group ATT 4 weeks”

mediators_claimed: Institutional amplification and information diffusion: libraries, bookstores and media responding to the award with advertising, favorable placement and media attention

evidence.annotation: Note: Fig. 2 shows ATT event study estimates from difference-in-differences models of the effect of literary awards on loan of library books. The shaded area shows 95% confidence interval. Panel A depicts the effect on the award-winning book. Panel B depicts a “spill-over” effect on other books by the same author. value.claimed_domain: The impact of signals from cultural intermediaries on cultural consumption; the author frames free library lending as a “most likely” case, where the cost of letting intermediaries sway an uncertain choice is lower than for purchases of books, art or concerts.
boundary_conditions: Library use is a “most likely” case because access is free and consumption barriers are low
Library books likely contribute differently to reading practices than purchased books

anchor_quote.text: To estimate the impact of literary awards, I use a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) design and compare loans of books before and after the announcement of a literary award, to a control group consisting of nominated/short-listed …

claims.statement: Over the 26 weeks following the event, literary award with high cultural legitimacy (“Award by committee”) increases number of loans per title per week of the award-winning title (“Award title”).

treatment.label: Literary award with high cultural legitimacy (“Award by committee”)

register_source.value: Dataset on major Danish literary awards announced from July 2021 to December 2022, merged to the library loan data by title and by author; not a Statistics Denmark register

definition.value: Award whose final decision is made by an appointed committee of literary professionals; the paper defines these as awards with high cultural legitimacy. The sample is split on this indicator and the award treatment re-estimated within the split.

timing.value: Week in which the award is announced; treatment is staggered across award events (14 awards on 18 award-winning titles in the award-title analysis)

outcome.label: Number of loans per title per week of the award-winning title (“Award title”)

register_source.value: Registry data on the universe of library book loans from Danish public libraries (book title, author, date of loan, personal identifier of the loaner)

definition.value: Weekly count of loans of the book title from Danish public libraries. Table 2 states the unit as “Number of loans per title”; the text reports the effect as books per title per week.

timing.value: Weekly, in event time relative to the week of the award/review; aggregated over the 26-week (half a year) post-period

units.value: number of loans per title per week

estimand.time_horizon: group-averaged ATT over the 26-week (half a year) post-period (long-term)

population.description: Loans of award-winning titles and of control titles (nominated/short-listed titles and titles awarded later), from the universe of adults’ loans of books (excluding children’s books) from Danish public libraries, May 2021 to December 2022, restricted to awards whose final decision is made by an appointed committee
population.ages: Adults (the paper analyses adults’ loans of books, excluding children’s books)
population.period: May 2021 to December 2022 (loans); awards/reviews from July 2021 to December 2022
population.selection: Only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point enter the sample, so treated and control titles are “equally selected”; titles enter the dataset the first week a loan is observed.

identification.source_of_variation: Staggered timing of the announcement of major Danish literary awards (14 award events in the award-title analysis, July 2021 to December 2022), compared with nominated/short-listed titles and titles that win an award later (not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the award/review, loans of treated titles would have followed the same average time path as loans of the control titles (nominated/short-listed and not-yet-treated titles).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper motivates the control group as netting out average time trends and presents dynamic event studies with pre-award event time (Fig. 2, Fig. 4, Fig. 5); it notes awards occur about a year after publication, which enables estimating a pre-trend.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on ever being treated or nominated: only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point are compared, so that treated and control books are “equally selected” on the characteristics that make a book award-worthy.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the construction of the control group; no balance test is reported.

implies_edges.from: Sample inclusion: ever awarded/nominated (awards) or ever reviewed (reviews)
implies_edges.to: Number of loans per title per week of the award-winning title (“Award title”)

key_assumptions.supported_by: Robustness analysis dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3 and Appendix Fig. A4); results reported as robust.

implies_edges.from: Literary award with high cultural legitimacy (“Award by committee”)
implies_edges.to: Loans of control titles (nominated / not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: loans do not respond to the award/review before the week it is announced or published.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Not tested directly; the event-study figures display pre-event event-time estimates.

implies_edges.from: Literary award with high cultural legitimacy (“Award by committee”)
implies_edges.to: Number of loans per title per week of the award-winning title (“Award title”) (pre-announcement weeks)

key_assumptions.assumption: Libraries do not differentially increase the physical/digital supply of award-winning books relative to control books in a way that generates the loan increase.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued rather than tested: the paper says library book purchasing agreements are a fairly slow process that cannot explain spikes in loans a few weeks after an award.

threats_discussed: Non-random timing of awards (awards may be announced when loans would be high anyway)
Non-random selection of books into awards (genre, quality, style)
Nominated control titles are themselves “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced
Supply constraints on physical and digital loans, and possible library supply responses to awards
robustness_checks: Dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A4)
Adding a third “mixed” cultural-legitimacy category (Appendix Figure A1)
Restricting to individuals who used libraries at least once in 2020 (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A5)
Measuring the outcome in logs rather than levels (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A9)
Survey-based measure of reading practices from the Cultural Participation Survey (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Fig. A2-A3)
Narrower cultural-elite definitions: PhD degree and top 5th percentile of library users (Appendix Tables A1 and A2, Appendix Fig. A8)
Stratification by income and by cultural/economic capital of occupation (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Figure A3)

claims.statement: Over the 4 weeks following the event, literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award) increases number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group, for the award-winning title (“Award title”) among individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college.

treatment.label: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award)

register_source.value: Dataset on major Danish literary awards announced from July 2021 to December 2022, merged to the library loan data by title and by author; not a Statistics Denmark register

definition.value: A binary, staggered treatment switching on in the week a major Danish literary award is announced. Awards announced July 2021 to December 2022 (e.g. De Gyldne Laurbær, Nordisk Råds Litteraturpris, Politikens Litteraturpris); 14 award events in the award-title analysis. Awards are merged to the loan data both by title and by author.

timing.value: Week in which the award is announced; treatment is staggered across award events (14 awards on 18 award-winning titles in the award-title analysis)

outcome.label: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group, for the award-winning title (“Award title”)

register_source.value: Registry data on the universe of library book loans from Danish public libraries (book title, author, date of loan, personal identifier of the loaner); linked via unique personal identifiers to the Danish national registries for the loaner’s highest education and previous library use

definition.value: Weekly count of loans of the book title made by members of the stratifying group, scaled by the group population count and expressed per 100,000 persons. Table 3 prints the unit as “losans per title per 100,00 person”; the text states “the number of books loaned per week per 100,000 person”.

timing.value: Weekly, in event time relative to the week of the award/review; aggregated over the first 4 weeks post-period

units.value: loans per week per 100,000 persons in the group

estimand.target_population: Treated titles in the individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college stratum
estimand.time_horizon: group-averaged ATT over the 4 weeks after the award/review (short-term)

population.description: Loans of award-winning titles and of control titles (nominated/short-listed titles and titles awarded later), from the universe of adults’ loans of books (excluding children’s books) from Danish public libraries, May 2021 to December 2022, restricted to loans made by individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college
population.ages: Adults (the paper analyses adults’ loans of books, excluding children’s books)
population.period: May 2021 to December 2022 (loans); awards/reviews from July 2021 to December 2022
population.selection: Only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point enter the sample, so treated and control titles are “equally selected”; titles enter the dataset the first week a loan is observed. Loans are further restricted to those made by individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college.

identification.source_of_variation: Staggered timing of the announcement of major Danish literary awards (14 award events in the award-title analysis, July 2021 to December 2022), compared with nominated/short-listed titles and titles that win an award later (not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the award/review, loans of treated titles would have followed the same average time path as loans of the control titles (nominated/short-listed and not-yet-treated titles).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper motivates the control group as netting out average time trends and presents dynamic event studies with pre-award event time (Fig. 2, Fig. 4, Fig. 5); it notes awards occur about a year after publication, which enables estimating a pre-trend.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on ever being treated or nominated: only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point are compared, so that treated and control books are “equally selected” on the characteristics that make a book award-worthy.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the construction of the control group; no balance test is reported.

implies_edges.from: Sample inclusion: ever awarded/nominated (awards) or ever reviewed (reviews)
implies_edges.to: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group, for the award-winning title (“Award title”)

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference: the award/review event does not itself change loans of the control titles (the paper concedes that nominated control titles are “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Robustness analysis dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3 and Appendix Fig. A4); results reported as robust.

implies_edges.from: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award)
implies_edges.to: Loans of control titles (nominated / not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: loans do not respond to the award/review before the week it is announced or published.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Not tested directly; the event-study figures display pre-event event-time estimates.

implies_edges.from: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award)
implies_edges.to: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group, for the award-winning title (“Award title”) (pre-announcement weeks)

key_assumptions.assumption: Libraries do not differentially increase the physical/digital supply of award-winning books relative to control books in a way that generates the loan increase.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued rather than tested: the paper says library book purchasing agreements are a fairly slow process that cannot explain spikes in loans a few weeks after an award.

threats_discussed: Non-random timing of awards (awards may be announced when loans would be high anyway)
Non-random selection of books into awards (genre, quality, style)
Nominated control titles are themselves “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced
Supply constraints on physical and digital loans, and possible library supply responses to awards
robustness_checks: Dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A4)
Adding a third “mixed” cultural-legitimacy category (Appendix Figure A1)
Restricting to individuals who used libraries at least once in 2020 (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A5)
Measuring the outcome in logs rather than levels (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A9)
Survey-based measure of reading practices from the Cultural Participation Survey (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Fig. A2-A3)
Narrower cultural-elite definitions: PhD degree and top 5th percentile of library users (Appendix Tables A1 and A2, Appendix Fig. A8)
Stratification by income and by cultural/economic capital of occupation (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Figure A3)
unresolved_confounders: The effect cannot be decomposed into the direct effect of individuals noticing the signal and the indirect effect of institutions (libraries, bookstores, media) amplifying it
Group differences may reflect heterogeneity in exposure to the signal (reading the right newspapers, seeing the right library exhibits) rather than differential responsiveness
The paper cannot test whether low effects among non-readers and the less educated reflect rejection of intermediaries’ legitimacy or simply being uninformed

treatment.label: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award) — received by the author of the book (spill-over)

register_source.value: Dataset on major Danish literary awards announced from July 2021 to December 2022, merged to the library loan data by title and by author; not a Statistics Denmark register

definition.value: A binary, staggered treatment switching on in the week a major Danish literary award is announced. Awards announced July 2021 to December 2022 (e.g. De Gyldne Laurbær, Nordisk Råds Litteraturpris, Politikens Litteraturpris); 14 award events in the award-title analysis. Awards are merged to the loan data both by title and by author. In this sample the treated books are other books by the award-winning author, so the award is received by the author rather than by the book itself.

timing.value: Week in which the award is announced; treatment is staggered across award events (14 awards on 18 award-winning titles in the award-title analysis)

outcome.label: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group, for other books by the award-winning author (“Award author”)

register_source.value: Registry data on the universe of library book loans from Danish public libraries (book title, author, date of loan, personal identifier of the loaner); linked via unique personal identifiers to the Danish national registries for the loaner’s highest education and previous library use

definition.value: Weekly count of loans of the book title made by members of the stratifying group, scaled by the group population count and expressed per 100,000 persons. Table 3 prints the unit as “losans per title per 100,00 person”; the text states “the number of books loaned per week per 100,000 person”.

timing.value: Weekly, in event time relative to the week of the award/review; aggregated over the first 4 weeks post-period

units.value: loans per week per 100,000 persons in the group

estimand.target_population: Other books by treated authors in the individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college stratum
estimand.time_horizon: group-averaged ATT over the 4 weeks after the award/review (short-term)

population.description: Loans of other books by award-winning authors and of control titles (nominated/short-listed titles and titles awarded later), from the universe of adults’ loans of books (excluding children’s books) from Danish public libraries, May 2021 to December 2022, restricted to loans made by individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college
population.ages: Adults (the paper analyses adults’ loans of books, excluding children’s books)
population.period: May 2021 to December 2022 (loans); awards/reviews from July 2021 to December 2022
population.selection: Only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point enter the sample, so treated and control titles are “equally selected”; titles enter the dataset the first week a loan is observed. Loans are further restricted to those made by individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college.

identification.source_of_variation: Staggered timing of the announcement of major Danish literary awards (14 award events in the award-title analysis, July 2021 to December 2022), compared with nominated/short-listed titles and titles that win an award later (not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the award/review, loans of treated titles would have followed the same average time path as loans of the control titles (nominated/short-listed and not-yet-treated titles).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper motivates the control group as netting out average time trends and presents dynamic event studies with pre-award event time (Fig. 2, Fig. 4, Fig. 5); it notes awards occur about a year after publication, which enables estimating a pre-trend.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on ever being treated or nominated: only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point are compared, so that treated and control books are “equally selected” on the characteristics that make a book award-worthy.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the construction of the control group; no balance test is reported.

implies_edges.from: Sample inclusion: ever awarded/nominated (awards) or ever reviewed (reviews)
implies_edges.to: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group, for other books by the award-winning author (“Award author”)

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference: the award/review event does not itself change loans of the control titles (the paper concedes that nominated control titles are “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Robustness analysis dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3 and Appendix Fig. A4); results reported as robust.

implies_edges.from: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award) — received by the author of the book (spill-over)
implies_edges.to: Loans of control titles (nominated / not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: loans do not respond to the award/review before the week it is announced or published.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Not tested directly; the event-study figures display pre-event event-time estimates.

implies_edges.from: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award) — received by the author of the book (spill-over)
implies_edges.to: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group, for other books by the award-winning author (“Award author”) (pre-announcement weeks)

key_assumptions.assumption: Libraries do not differentially increase the physical/digital supply of award-winning books relative to control books in a way that generates the loan increase.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued rather than tested: the paper says library book purchasing agreements are a fairly slow process that cannot explain spikes in loans a few weeks after an award.

threats_discussed: Non-random timing of awards (awards may be announced when loans would be high anyway)
Non-random selection of books into awards (genre, quality, style)
Nominated control titles are themselves “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced
Supply constraints on physical and digital loans, and possible library supply responses to awards
robustness_checks: Dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A4)
Adding a third “mixed” cultural-legitimacy category (Appendix Figure A1)
Restricting to individuals who used libraries at least once in 2020 (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A5)
Measuring the outcome in logs rather than levels (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A9)
Survey-based measure of reading practices from the Cultural Participation Survey (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Fig. A2-A3)
Narrower cultural-elite definitions: PhD degree and top 5th percentile of library users (Appendix Tables A1 and A2, Appendix Fig. A8)
Stratification by income and by cultural/economic capital of occupation (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Figure A3)
unresolved_confounders: The effect cannot be decomposed into the direct effect of individuals noticing the signal and the indirect effect of institutions (libraries, bookstores, media) amplifying it
Group differences may reflect heterogeneity in exposure to the signal (reading the right newspapers, seeing the right library exhibits) rather than differential responsiveness
The paper cannot test whether low effects among non-readers and the less educated reflect rejection of intermediaries’ legitimacy or simply being uninformed

estimator.value: Staggered difference-in-differences, Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021) group-time ATT, aggregated to a group-averaged ATT

estimation.specification: Staggered DID on weekly loans per title; group-time ATT(g,t) à la Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021) with nominated/short-listed and not-yet-treated titles as controls, aggregated to a group-averaged ATT over the first 4 weeks post-period. No estimating equation is printed in the paper.
estimation.weights: Outcome scaled by the stratifying group’s population count (expressed per 100,000 persons); no estimation weights are described

source_table.value: Table 3, row “Award author / 5 + y. College”, column “Group ATT 4 weeks”

mediators_claimed: Institutional amplification and information diffusion: libraries, bookstores and media responding to the award with advertising, favorable placement and media attention

heterogeneity.finding: This group is the reference category (REF) in the “Dif 4 weeks” column of Table 3; the other groups’ ATTs are tested against it with Z tests.

Awards announced July 2021 to December 2022 (e.g. De Gyldne Laurbær, Nordisk Råds Litteraturpris, Politikens Litteraturpris); 14 award events in the award-title analysis. Awards are merged to the loan data both by title and by author. In this sample the treated books are other books by the award-winning author, so the award is received by the author rather than by the book itself.

timing.value: Week in which the award is announced; treatment is staggered across award events (14 awards on 18 award-winning titles in the award-title analysis)

outcome.label: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group; the Outcome column prints “Award title” for this row, but it sits in the second (Award author / spill-over) block of Table 3

register_source.value: Registry data on the universe of library book loans from Danish public libraries (book title, author, date of loan, personal identifier of the loaner); linked via unique personal identifiers to the Danish national registries for the loaner’s highest education and previous library use

definition.value: Weekly count of loans of the book title made by members of the stratifying group, scaled by the group population count and expressed per 100,000 persons. Table 3 prints the unit as “losans per title per 100,00 person”; the text states “the number of books loaned per week per 100,000 person”.

timing.value: Weekly, in event time relative to the week of the award/review; aggregated over the first 4 weeks post-period

units.value: loans per week per 100,000 persons in the group

estimand.target_population: Other books by treated authors in the individuals at or above the 75th percentile of books loaned from libraries in 2020 (17 books or more) stratum
estimand.time_horizon: group-averaged ATT over the 4 weeks after the award/review (short-term)

population.description: Loans of other books by award-winning authors and of control titles (nominated/short-listed titles and titles awarded later), from the universe of adults’ loans of books (excluding children’s books) from Danish public libraries, May 2021 to December 2022, restricted to loans made by individuals at or above the 75th percentile of books loaned from libraries in 2020 (17 books or more)
population.ages: Adults (the paper analyses adults’ loans of books, excluding children’s books)
population.period: May 2021 to December 2022 (loans); awards/reviews from July 2021 to December 2022
population.selection: Only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point enter the sample, so treated and control titles are “equally selected”; titles enter the dataset the first week a loan is observed. Loans are further restricted to those made by individuals at or above the 75th percentile of books loaned from libraries in 2020 (17 books or more).

identification.source_of_variation: Staggered timing of the announcement of major Danish literary awards (14 award events in the award-title analysis, July 2021 to December 2022), compared with nominated/short-listed titles and titles that win an award later (not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the award/review, loans of treated titles would have followed the same average time path as loans of the control titles (nominated/short-listed and not-yet-treated titles).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper motivates the control group as netting out average time trends and presents dynamic event studies with pre-award event time (Fig. 2, Fig. 4, Fig. 5); it notes awards occur about a year after publication, which enables estimating a pre-trend.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on ever being treated or nominated: only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point are compared, so that treated and control books are “equally selected” on the characteristics that make a book award-worthy.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the construction of the control group; no balance test is reported.

implies_edges.to: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group; the Outcome column prints “Award title” for this row, but it sits in the second (Award author / spill-over) block of Table 3

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference: the award/review event does not itself change loans of the control titles (the paper concedes that nominated control titles are “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Robustness analysis dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3 and Appendix Fig. A4); results reported as robust.

implies_edges.from: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award) — received by the author of the book (spill-over)
implies_edges.to: Loans of control titles (nominated / not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: loans do not respond to the award/review before the week it is announced or published.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Not tested directly; the event-study figures display pre-event event-time estimates.

implies_edges.from: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award) — received by the author of the book (spill-over)
implies_edges.to: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group; the Outcome column prints “Award title” for this row, but it sits in the second (Award author / spill-over) block of Table 3 (pre-announcement weeks)

key_assumptions.assumption: Libraries do not differentially increase the physical/digital supply of award-winning books relative to control books in a way that generates the loan increase.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued rather than tested: the paper says library book purchasing agreements are a fairly slow process that cannot explain spikes in loans a few weeks after an award.

threats_discussed: Non-random timing of awards (awards may be announced when loans would be high anyway)
Non-random selection of books into awards (genre, quality, style)
Nominated control titles are themselves “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced
Supply constraints on physical and digital loans, and possible library supply responses to awards
robustness_checks: Dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A4)
Adding a third “mixed” cultural-legitimacy category (Appendix Figure A1)
Restricting to individuals who used libraries at least once in 2020 (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A5)
Measuring the outcome in logs rather than levels (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A9)
Survey-based measure of reading practices from the Cultural Participation Survey (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Fig. A2-A3)
Narrower cultural-elite definitions: PhD degree and top 5th percentile of library users (Appendix Tables A1 and A2, Appendix Fig. A8)
Stratification by income and by cultural/economic capital of occupation (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Figure A3)
unresolved_confounders: The effect cannot be decomposed into the direct effect of individuals noticing the signal and the indirect effect of institutions (libraries, bookstores, media) amplifying it
Group differences may reflect heterogeneity in exposure to the signal (reading the right newspapers, seeing the right library exhibits) rather than differential responsiveness
The paper cannot test whether low effects among non-readers and the less educated reflect rejection of intermediaries’ legitimacy or simply being uninformed

treatment.label: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award) — received by the author of the book (spill-over)

register_source.value: Dataset on major Danish literary awards announced from July 2021 to December 2022, merged to the library loan data by title and by author; not a Statistics Denmark register

definition.value: A binary, staggered treatment switching on in the week a major Danish literary award is announced. Awards announced July 2021 to December 2022 (e.g. De Gyldne Laurbær, Nordisk Råds Litteraturpris, Politikens Litteraturpris); 14 award events in the award-title analysis. Awards are merged to the loan data both by title and by author. In this sample the treated books are other books by the award-winning author, so the award is received by the author rather than by the book itself.

timing.value: Week in which the award is announced; treatment is staggered across award events (14 awards on 18 award-winning titles in the award-title analysis)

outcome.label: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group; the Outcome column prints “Award title” for this row, but it sits in the second (Award author / spill-over) block of Table 3

register_source.value: Registry data on the universe of library book loans from Danish public libraries (book title, author, date of loan, personal identifier of the loaner); linked via unique personal identifiers to the Danish national registries for the loaner’s highest education and previous library use

definition.value: Weekly count of loans of the book title made by members of the stratifying group, scaled by the group population count and expressed per 100,000 persons. Table 3 prints the unit as “losans per title per 100,00 person”; the text states “the number of books loaned per week per 100,000 person”.

timing.value: Weekly, in event time relative to the week of the award/review; aggregated over the 26-week (half a year) post-period

units.value: loans per week per 100,000 persons in the group

estimand.target_population: Other books by treated authors in the individuals who had no loan of books from libraries in 2020 stratum
estimand.time_horizon: group-averaged ATT over the 26-week (half a year) post-period (long-term)

population.description: Loans of other books by award-winning authors and of control titles (nominated/short-listed titles and titles awarded later), from the universe of adults’ loans of books (excluding children’s books) from Danish public libraries, May 2021 to December 2022, restricted to loans made by individuals who had no loan of books from libraries in 2020
population.ages: Adults (the paper analyses adults’ loans of books, excluding children’s books)
population.period: May 2021 to December 2022 (loans); awards/reviews from July 2021 to December 2022
population.selection: Only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point enter the sample, so treated and control titles are “equally selected”; titles enter the dataset the first week a loan is observed. Loans are further restricted to those made by individuals who had no loan of books from libraries in 2020.

identification.source_of_variation: Staggered timing of the announcement of major Danish literary awards (14 award events in the award-title analysis, July 2021 to December 2022), compared with nominated/short-listed titles and titles that win an award later (not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the award/review, loans of treated titles would have followed the same average time path as loans of the control titles (nominated/short-listed and not-yet-treated titles).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper motivates the control group as netting out average time trends and presents dynamic event studies with pre-award event time (Fig. 2, Fig. 4, Fig. 5); it notes awards occur about a year after publication, which enables estimating a pre-trend.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on ever being treated or nominated: only books that receive or are nominated/short-listed for an award at some point are compared, so that treated and control books are “equally selected” on the characteristics that make a book award-worthy.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the construction of the control group; no balance test is reported.

implies_edges.from: Sample inclusion: ever awarded/nominated (awards) or ever reviewed (reviews)
implies_edges.to: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group; the Outcome column prints “Award title” for this row, but it sits in the second (Award author / spill-over) block of Table 3

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference: the award/review event does not itself change loans of the control titles (the paper concedes that nominated control titles are “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Robustness analysis dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3 and Appendix Fig. A4); results reported as robust.

implies_edges.from: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award) — received by the author of the book (spill-over)
implies_edges.to: Loans of control titles (nominated / not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: loans do not respond to the award/review before the week it is announced or published.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Not tested directly; the event-study figures display pre-event event-time estimates.

implies_edges.from: Literary award (announcement of a major Danish literary award) — received by the author of the book (spill-over)
implies_edges.to: Number of books loaned per week per 100,000 persons in the group; the Outcome column prints “Award title” for this row, but it sits in the second (Award author / spill-over) block of Table 3 (pre-announcement weeks)

key_assumptions.assumption: Libraries do not differentially increase the physical/digital supply of award-winning books relative to control books in a way that generates the loan increase.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued rather than tested: the paper says library book purchasing agreements are a fairly slow process that cannot explain spikes in loans a few weeks after an award.

threats_discussed: Non-random timing of awards (awards may be announced when loans would be high anyway)
Non-random selection of books into awards (genre, quality, style)
Nominated control titles are themselves “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced
Supply constraints on physical and digital loans, and possible library supply responses to awards
robustness_checks: Dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A4)
Adding a third “mixed” cultural-legitimacy category (Appendix Figure A1)
Restricting to individuals who used libraries at least once in 2020 (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A5)
Measuring the outcome in logs rather than levels (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A9)
Survey-based measure of reading practices from the Cultural Participation Survey (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Fig. A2-A3)
Narrower cultural-elite definitions: PhD degree and top 5th percentile of library users (Appendix Tables A1 and A2, Appendix Fig. A8)
Stratification by income and by cultural/economic capital of occupation (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Figure A3)
unresolved_confounders: The effect cannot be decomposed into the direct effect of individuals noticing the signal and the indirect effect of institutions (libraries, bookstores, media) amplifying it
Group differences may reflect heterogeneity in exposure to the signal (reading the right newspapers, seeing the right library exhibits) rather than differential responsiveness
The paper cannot test whether low effects among non-readers and the less educated reflect rejection of intermediaries’ legitimacy or simply being uninformed

estimator.value: Staggered difference-in-differences, Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021) group-time ATT, aggregated to a group-averaged ATT

estimation.specification: Staggered DID on weekly loans per title; group-time ATT(g,t) à la Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021) with nominated/short-listed and not-yet-treated titles as controls, aggregated to a group-averaged ATT over the 26-week post-period. No estimating equation is printed in the paper.
estimation.weights: Outcome scaled by the stratifying group’s population count (expressed per 100,000 persons); no estimation weights are described

source_table.value: Table 3, row “Award title (second block) / Non-readers”, column “Group ATT 26 weeks”

mediators_claimed: Institutional amplification and information diffusion: libraries, bookstores and media responding to the award with advertising, favorable placement and media attention

heterogeneity.finding: Table 3, “Dif 26 weeks” is blank for this row: the ATT is not statistically significantly different from the reference group (Avid readers).

claims.statement: Over the 4 weeks following the event, positive literary review in a national Danish newspaper increases loans per 100,000 persons in the group, of other books by the reviewed author among individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college.

treatment.label: Positive literary review in a national Danish newspaper

register_source.value: Dataset of literary reviews in national Danish newspapers (July 2021 to December 2022) collected from the website Bog.nu; not a Statistics Denmark register

definition.value: The author receives a newspaper literary review with a normalized book score rating (1–100) above the 75th percentile; reviews collected from the website Bog.nu for July 2021 to December 2022. Treatment is staggered by the week the review is published.

timing.value: Week in which the review is published; treatment is staggered across review events, with not-yet-reviewed authors’ books as controls

outcome.label: Loans per 100,000 persons in the group, of other books by the reviewed author

register_source.value: Registry data on the universe of library book loans from Danish public libraries (book title, author, date of loan, personal identifier of the loaner); linked via unique personal identifiers to the Danish national registries for the loaner’s highest education and previous library use

definition.value: Loans of other books by the reviewed author made by members of the stratifying group, scaled by the group population count; Table 4 prints the unit as “Loans per 100,000”.

timing.value: Weekly, in event time relative to the week of the award/review; aggregated over the first 4 weeks post-period

units.value: loans per week per 100,000 persons in the group

estimand.target_population: Other books by treated authors in the individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college stratum
estimand.time_horizon: group-averaged ATT over the 4 weeks after the award/review (short-term)

population.description: Loans of other books by authors reviewed in national Danish newspapers, July 2021 to December 2022, from the universe of adults’ loans of books (excluding children’s books) from Danish public libraries, May 2021 to December 2022, restricted to loans made by individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college
population.ages: Adults (the paper analyses adults’ loans of books, excluding children’s books)
population.period: May 2021 to December 2022 (loans); awards/reviews from July 2021 to December 2022
population.selection: Books by authors who receive a newspaper literary review during the period; the reviewed book itself is excluded because reviews are published around the time the book becomes available, so only the spill-over sample is analysed. Control books are not-yet-treated. Loans are further restricted to those made by individuals whose highest completed educational level is 5 or more years of college.

identification.source_of_variation: Staggered timing of the publication of literary reviews in national Danish newspapers (210 review events, July 2021 to December 2022), compared with not-yet-reviewed authors’ books over the same weeks

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the award/review, loans of treated titles would have followed the same average time path as loans of the control titles (nominated/short-listed and not-yet-treated titles).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper motivates the control group as netting out average time trends and presents dynamic event studies with pre-award event time (Fig. 6); it notes awards occur about a year after publication, which enables estimating a pre-trend.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on the author ever receiving a newspaper review in the period, and on the book not being the reviewed book itself; controls are not-yet-reviewed.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the construction of the control group; no balance test is reported.

implies_edges.from: Sample inclusion: ever awarded/nominated (awards) or ever reviewed (reviews)
implies_edges.to: Loans per 100,000 persons in the group, of other books by the reviewed author

key_assumptions.supported_by: Robustness analysis dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3 and Appendix Fig. A4); results reported as robust.

implies_edges.from: Positive literary review in a national Danish newspaper
implies_edges.to: Loans of control titles (nominated / not-yet-treated)

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: loans do not respond to the award/review before the week it is announced or published.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Not tested directly; the event-study figures display pre-event event-time estimates.

implies_edges.from: Positive literary review in a national Danish newspaper
implies_edges.to: Loans per 100,000 persons in the group, of other books by the reviewed author (pre-announcement weeks)

threats_discussed: Non-random timing of awards (awards may be announced when loans would be high anyway)
Non-random selection of books into awards (genre, quality, style)
Nominated control titles are themselves “in some sense” treated when nominations are announced
robustness_checks: Dropping nominated titles from the control group (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A4)
Adding a third “mixed” cultural-legitimacy category (Appendix Figure A1)
Restricting to individuals who used libraries at least once in 2020 (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A5)
Measuring the outcome in logs rather than levels (Appendix Table A3, Appendix Fig. A9)
Survey-based measure of reading practices from the Cultural Participation Survey (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Fig. A2-A3)

Stratification by income and by cultural/economic capital of occupation (Appendix Table A1-A2, Appendix Figure A3)

Group differences may reflect heterogeneity in exposure to the signal (reading the right newspapers, seeing the right library exhibits) rather than differential responsiveness
The paper cannot test whether low effects among non-readers and the less educated reflect rejection of intermediaries’ legitimacy or simply being uninformed

evidence.annotation: Note: Fig. 6 shows ATT event study estimates from difference-in-differences models of the effect of literary reviews in national newspapers on loan of library books. The shaded area shows 95% confidence interval. Panel A depicts a “spill-over” effect of a positive review on other books by the same author. Panel B compares the effect of a positive, mediocre, and negative review. Panel C splits the effect by education. Panel D splits the effect by previous library use. Note that the Y axis differs between Panels A to D.
